extracted.intended_audience: machine learning researchers (authors), conference reviewers, and conference organizers implementing reproducibility practices
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for improving reproducibility of ML research in the context of a conference (NeurIPS 2019): code/data submission policy, a community reproducibility challenge, and a Machine Learning reproducibility checklist to be filled by authors and used by reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code submission policy (quoted)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Authors may submit up to 100MB of supplementary material, such as proofs, derivations, data, or source code." "To foster reproducibility, we highly encourage authors to submit code. Reproducibility of results and easy availability of code will be taken into account in the decision-making process." "We expect (but not require) accompanying code to be submitted with accepted papers that contribute and present experiments with a new algorithm."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy is encouragement rather than coercion: code is expected for accepted papers by camera-ready deadline but not mandatory at submission; authors may provide links to repositories at submission; code availability may be considered by reviewers but is not required to decide acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide code (availability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the code used to run experiments (link in submission or supplementary material; ideally a repository with DOI for final version).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encouraged to upload to a repository and give a DOI; authors from industry or with proprietary constraints should still consider providing complementary experiments on open benchmarks; reviewers were asked to indicate if code was provided and whether they consulted it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide data or note dataset confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Make data publicly available where possible; if dataset confidentiality prevents sharing, mitigate by providing complementary empirical results on an open-source benchmark dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If data cannot be released for legitimate privacy reasons (e.g., healthcare, finance), document this and provide as much alternative evidence as possible that allows verification and comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear description of mathematical setting / algorithm / model
rubrics_metrics.description: Q#. A clear description of the mathematical setting, algorithm, and/or model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is expected for almost all submissions; authors should ensure explicit formalization so others can reproduce the implementation from the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of how experiments were run (experimental protocol)
rubrics_metrics.description: Q#. For all figures and tables that present empirical results, indicate if you include: A description of how experiments were run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include commands, environment, random seeds, hardware, software stack, training procedure, and any pre-/post-processing steps. This enables re-running the experiments or reimplementing with fidelity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear definition of measures / statistics used
rubrics_metrics.description: Q#. A clear definition of the specific measure or statistics used to report results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precisely define metrics, loss functions, evaluation criteria, and any transforms applied to scores. Ambiguous or unspecified metrics hamper reproducibility and comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include error bars when applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Q#. Clearly defined error bars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report uncertainty measures (error bars) for empirical results when variability exists. The checklist revealed many papers considered error bars 'not applicable' — authors should justify when they are omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report central tendency and variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Q#. A description of results with central tendency (e.g. mean) & variation (e.g. stddev).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report means and standard deviations (or appropriate robust statistics) across multiple runs/initializations; indicate number of repeats and whether results are aggregated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper use of statistics and significance testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use appropriate statistical analysis to quantify uncertainty and support claims (avoid claiming significance without proper testing or using wrong statistical tests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply correct hypothesis testing, multiple-comparison corrections when needed, and avoid over-interpreting small differences; explicitly report tests used and p-values or confidence intervals where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report train / validation / test splits
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist items related to test/validation/train splits should be documented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State how data was partitioned, whether splits are random or fixed, whether any data leakage exists, and how hyperparameter tuning avoided contamination of test data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report hyper-parameter ranges and search details
rubrics_metrics.description: Include hyper-parameter ranges and search strategy (grid/search/random/bayesian), and report best settings used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document search ranges, number of trials, selection criteria, and whether reported results are from hyperparameter tuning on validation data; thorough hyper-parameter search can change relative method performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify number of runs and treatment of randomness (random seeds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for randomness (e.g., random initializations) by running multiple trials and reporting variability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report number of seeds/trials, use of deterministic settings when possible, and aggregate statistics. Several cited studies show performance can vary across initializations — single-run reporting is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid under-specification of model or training procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not leave model architecture, training procedure, optimization details, or implementation choices under-specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient implementation detail so reimplementers can recover the method; missing details often prevent reproduction even if code is unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid selective reporting and adaptive overfitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid selectively reporting only positive results or tuning to benchmarks in a way that inflates claims (adaptive overfitting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report negative results, ablations, and full experimental regimes. When multiple variants were tried, disclose them and justify the chosen presentation to prevent misleading claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-claiming results beyond evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not draw conclusions that go beyond what the empirical evidence supports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame conclusions proportionally to the scope and limitations of experiments; be cautious about generalization claims without broad evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material size and content
rubrics_metrics.description: "Authors may submit up to 100MB of supplementary material, such as proofs, derivations, data, or source code."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use supplementary material to include proofs, derivations, datasets (as allowed), code snippets, and extended experimental details; adhere to platform limits and provide external repository links for larger artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document compute requirements and practicality of reproduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Document computation infrastructure needed to reproduce experiments, since some work may be impractical to rerun due to resource demands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report training time, number of GPUs/TPUs, memory, and any specialized hardware; if experiments are large-scale, provide smaller-scale experiments or checkpoints that allow partial verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide provenance and use reproducibility tooling where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider packaging experiments with tools (Docker, ReproZip, WholeTale) that encapsulate OS, code, dependencies, and data to aid long-term reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardize on tooling where possible and document usage instructions; a comparison of tools is cited to guide selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility report content and public archival
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproducibility reports should provide a detailed and nuanced account of reproduction attempts, include reimplementation code where possible, and record the level of fidelity to original methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make reports publicly available (e.g., OpenReview, ReScience); include links to code, description of deviations, results comparison, and discussion of obstacles encountered; avoid reducing findings to a single coarse 'reproducibility score.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of OpenReview / wiki interaction for reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Use public platforms (OpenReview) and wiki pages to enable interaction between authors and reproducers and to host reproduction notes and code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open communication accelerates pinpointing omissions and errors; community wikis per paper can collect code links, issues, and reproduction notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer reporting of artifact usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should indicate whether code was provided, if they looked at it, and whether the code was useful in guiding the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey responses suggested many reviewers wish code was available; reviewing artifacts can be optional but reviewers should report artifact engagement for analysis of policy impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation for code at camera-ready for accepted papers
rubrics_metrics.description: The policy: 'We expect (but not require) accompanying code to be submitted with accepted papers that contribute and present experiments with a new algorithm.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should plan to make code available by camera-ready when possible; this is not enforced for acceptance but is an expectation to improve the archival value of the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address proprietary software limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: If software contains intellectual property or depends on proprietary libraries, authors should acknowledge limitations and provide complementary open-benchmark results when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry authors may face IP constraints — document them and provide reproducible components or alternative experiments that can be inspected by reviewers and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage reproduction of accepted papers (targeted replication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproducibility challenges should focus effort on accepted papers to maximize impact; participants claim papers for reproduction and publish detailed reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers should enable claim lists, provide compute support when possible (e.g., CodeOcean), and arrange peer-review of reproducibility reports to produce archival records (e.g., ReScience).

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist usage and form
rubrics_metrics.description: Machine Learning Reproducibility Checklist (v1.2): a set of yes/no/not applicable questions (with optional comments) about reporting items (math description, experimental details, metrics, error bars, etc.) required at initial submission and camera-ready.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors fill it at submission and camera-ready to track improvements; reviewers may find it useful (34% reported it was useful), and checklist answers often correlate with acceptance but should be interpreted with caution (covariates may exist).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely solely on code — value reimplementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of code is not a guarantee of correctness; reimplementation from a clear description is valuable to assess robustness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage both availability of original code and independent reimplementation efforts; both help surface mistakes and increase confidence in results.
